issues.quote: I never look at clocks when I am playing with Casimir. It is the only way I have ever won.
issues.fact: The sheet says only that she did not look at the clock when Casimir went out for cigars. It gives no general habit of not looking at clocks during play.
issues.misreading: A solver could take this as a general admission that her timekeeping through the whole piquet game is unreliable, so the temple's ten o'clock strike and the length of play before he left become doubtful. That casts doubt on the sheet's timing beyond the single unobserved moment.

issues.quote: He said a watch that old should not be carried by a man who cannot wind it.
issues.fact: The sheet says only that Félix's watch showed twenty minutes to nine when the temple struck nine. It says nothing about the watch running slow, stopping, or being unwound.
issues.misreading: The remark could be read as a hint that Félix's watch had run down or was inaccurate, so the twenty-to-nine reading might not be trustworthy. The sheet does not support that.
